headline: Likud claims Israel election 'stolen' by Arab parties, demands police/Shin Bet probe
dek: [ALLEGATION] Likud claims yesterday's election was 'stolen by Arab parties that support terror and the elimination of the Jewish state through serious criminal offenses of bribery, threats, violence, forgeries and the use of illegal software to mobilize voters,' and says it is handing police, the…
sources: Likud party statement via Times of Israel liveblog, Haaretz, Jerusalem Post, Ynetnews; Central Elections Committee statement via Times of Israel; absentee-pool update via The Times liveblog
fault_line: Fraud vs historic turnout: was the record Arab vote (19 seats) legitimate kingmaker power, or a stolen election that must be investigated before any government forms?

sections.what_happened: [ALLEGATION] Likud claims yesterday's election was 'stolen by Arab parties that support terror and the elimination of the Jewish state through serious criminal offenses of bribery, threats, violence, forgeries and the use of illegal software to mobilize voters,' and says it is handing police, the Shin Bet and the CEC 'hundreds of testimonies' plus 'thousands of envelopes with cash and Ra'am slips,' threats/violence toward ballot-committee members, multiple voters behind screens, double voting, envelope/voter-count discrepancies and illegal voter-mobilization software. [VERIFIED FACT] The CEC confirmed it received Likud's complaint and is reviewing it under its routine election-integrity monitoring operation (announced to all lists Oct 25), under which ALL parties' complaints are examined; it did not endorse the fraud claim. Standing count unchanged: 85.6% counted, Netanyahu bloc 53, Eisenkot bloc 48, Arab parties 19 (historic high), 61 needed. [ATTRIBUTED REPORT] The Times liveblog (crawled <1h before 22:00 ) puts remaining absentee ballots at 430,000-480,000, counted by Thursday afternoon -- NARROWER than the 600,000 double-envelope figure in the earlier ToI count item and the ~500,000 in Haaretz; treat the pool size as disputed until the CEC states it.
sections.what_verified: 4 distinct publisher families agree Likud made the claim and the CEC is reviewing it; all agree no evidence has been made public.
sections.what_disputed: Haaretz and Jerusalem Post both state explicitly that Likud provided NO evidence and no evidence establishing systematic manipulation has been made public. The CEC frames its review as the routine operation run after every election, not a fraud finding. The Arab parties' 19 seats follow record Arab turnout, the mechanism the claim disputes but does not evidence. The Times (London) liveblog is NOT in the source registry, so its 430k-480k absentee figure is reported with attribution only and does NOT count toward corroboration.
sections.why_matters: The count hasn't moved -- the fight has: loser cries stolen, election body opens the books. Lead with Likud's own 'stolen' quote, then the CEC's flat routine-review reply, then the 53-vs-61 maths. Proven-set adjacent (Israel election deadlock) with debate-bait fault line.
